```{=html}
<h2 class="lx-sr">Task</h2>
<div class="lx-card cka-intro">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">How this checkpoint works · about 150 minutes, no hints</p>
<ol class="cka-parts">
<li><b>A · Boundary and log</b> (about 40 min). Download the starter workbook. State your boundary; finish the assumptions log: every input's type, source, date and, where you will test it, a low and a high value.</li>
<li><b>B · The model</b> (about 50 min). Convert the costs to 2025 dollars and build the school's yearly saving and its <span class="lx-term" data-term="net-present-value">net present value</span> (NPV), every number a formula.</li>
<li><b>C · Who pays</b> (about 20 min). Split the school's bill saving into a real cost saved and a <span class="lx-term" data-term="transfer">transfer</span>; add the parties up (refresher: <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a>).</li>
<li><b>D · <span class="lx-term" data-term="sensitivity-analysis">Sensitivity</span></b> (about 20 min). Swing the inputs that matter one at a time and report the main result as a range.</li>
<li><b>Submit</b> (about 20 min). Enter your results in the nine tasks below, in any order: the worked workbook opens once all nine are answered.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">How it is marked, before you start</p>
<ul class="cka-rules">
<li><b>Proficient:</b> at least 5 of the 7 auto-marked tasks right on the first try, plus at least 3 of the 4 points of each written task (1 and 9), which you tick yourself.</li>
<li><b>Strong:</b> at least 6 of 7 on the first try and every written point.</li>
<li><b>Opening solutions early:</b> a task whose answer you open before answering counts as not right (a written task: no points). Opening the worked workbook before all nine are answered makes the attempt practice, with no level.</li>
<li><b>Written tasks:</b> your text stays as you first submit it, and that is the text you rate.</li>
<li><b>After the worked workbook opens:</b> an answer given after that counts as practice, not as right, and a written task then earns no points.</li>
</ul>
<p class="cka-dl"><a class="lx-btn small" href="../assets/learn/data/ck-a-starter.xlsx" download>Starter workbook (.xlsx)</a></p>
<p class="lx-hint">It opens in Excel, LibreOffice Calc, Google Sheets or Apple Numbers. It holds the case's facts with their sources and an empty layout: no formulas, no answers.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Refreshers: <a href="a01-project-tea.html">A1</a> (cash flows), <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a> (tariffs), <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a> (who pays), <a href="k03-discounting.html">K3</a> (discounting), <a href="k07-spreadsheets.html">K7</a> (spreadsheets).</p>
</div>

<div class="lx-card cka-brief" id="cka-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The case</p>
<h3>A school's rooftop solar and battery</h3>
<!-- cka-brief:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p><b>Situation:</b> Prairie Town High School's district is offered a rooftop solar array and a battery behind the school's meter.</p>
<p><b>Deliverable:</b> An auditable spreadsheet that tells the district what it would gain or lose, who else pays or benefits, and how sure that answer is.</p>
<p class="lx-eyebrow cka-in">Inputs, illustrative where marked</p>
<ul class="cka-facts"><li><b>System:</b> 250 <span class="lx-term" data-term="kw-dc">kW-DC</span> of rooftop solar and a 150 kW / 300 kWh battery, installed together</li><li><b>School:</b> uses 1,000,000 kWh a year, with a billed peak of 400 kW every month (illustrative)</li><li><b>Tariff:</b> a <span class="lx-term" data-term="demand-charge">demand charge</span> of $10 per kW-month plus an energy charge, set so the school's bill averages Kansas's 2025 commercial price, 11.17 cents/kWh (EIA); exports earn 3 cents/kWh (illustrative)</li><li><b>Battery power:</b> cuts the monthly billed peak by 60% of its power on average (illustrative)</li><li><b>Battery energy:</b> about 200 <span class="lx-term" data-term="full-cycle">full cycles</span> a year, each taking in 300 kWh from the school's supply and returning 90%; the 10% lost is bought at the energy charge (illustrative)</li><li><b>Costs:</b> from EIA's 2024 distributed-generation report (2022 dollars) and NLR's 2025 ATB (2023 dollars); convert to 2025 dollars</li><li><b>Money:</b> 25 years, real 2025 dollars, a 4% <span class="lx-term" data-term="real-rate">real discount rate</span> (the course's), battery replaced at the end of year 15</li><li><b>End value:</b> at year 25 the replacement battery has 5 of its 15 years left: count 5/15 of its cost as its <span class="lx-term" data-term="residual-value">residual value</span> (straight line)</li><li><b>The utility:</b> avoids 3 cents for each kWh it no longer supplies and, for half of the battery's peak cut, $180 per kW a year of capacity (illustrative; lesson A4's unit cost)</li><li><b>Rate reset:</b> assume the utility recovers its whole remaining revenue shortfall from its other customers at the next rate reset</li></ul>
<p class="lx-hint">Prairie Town and its high school are fictional; the school's load and several inputs are illustrative.</p>
<!-- cka-brief:end -->
</div>

<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="ck-a-spreadsheet" data-src="../assets/learn/data/ck-a-spreadsheet.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- cka-tasks:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-hint">Without JavaScript nothing here is locked: the worked solution is further down the page. Build your spreadsheet first, write your answers down, then compare.</p>
<ol class="cka-static">
<li><p><b>Your boundary</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A · State the boundary</span></p><p>In two or three sentences: whose money does your main result count, over what period and in which dollars, and what does it leave out?</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Solar output</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part B · A number with units</span></p><p>How much electricity does the array make in a year? Within 2% counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Up-front cost in 2025 dollars</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part B · Convert dollar years</span></p><p>What does the system cost up front, in 2025 dollars? Within 1% counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>The school's bill saving</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part B · Read a tariff</span></p><p>How much lower is the school's electricity bill in a year (gross: before upkeep)? Within 3% counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>The main result</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part B · Present value</span></p><p>Using the brief's assumptions, including its residual value, by how much does the present value of the school's costs exceed that of its savings? Within 3% counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Who pays the gap</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part C · Transfers against real costs</span></p><p>Part of the school's bill saving is not a saving in the utility's costs. Under the brief's rate-reset assumption, who pays it?</p><ul><li>a. The school district</li><li>b. The utility's other customers, at the next rate reset</li><li>c. Federal taxpayers</li><li>d. Nobody: every dollar the school saves is a real cost saved</li></ul></li>
<li><p><b>The cost shift</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part C · A screening estimate</span></p><p>Under the same assumption, how much a year moves to the utility's other customers? Within 5% counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>What moves the result most</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D · Sensitivity</span></p><p>Swinging one input at a time over the ranges in the worked log, which moves the school's NPV most?</p><ul><li>a. The up-front cost, ±25%</li><li>b. The discount rate, 2% to 7%</li><li>c. The demand charge, $5 to $20 per kW-month, with the energy charge re-set so the pre-project bill is unchanged</li><li>d. The average electricity price, ±20%</li></ul></li>
<li><p><b>Your log and your sensitivity</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D · Audit trail</span></p><p>Paste three rows of your assumptions log and your sensitivity statement (the main result as a range, and the input that moves it most).</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
</ol>
<!-- cka-tasks:end -->
</div>
</div>

Prices, costs, the <span class="lx-term" data-term="capacity-factor">capacity factor</span> and the price index are dated public figures (Sources).</span></p>
<p class="lx-datanote"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><span>Nothing you type leaves this browser unless you copy it. ## Worked solution
```
:::

```{=html}
<div id="cka-lock" class="lx-ck-lock" hidden>
<p><b>Opens once all nine tasks are answered.</b> The checkpoint asks for your own spreadsheet first, so the worked workbook waits for it. Opening it now makes this attempt practice, with no level.</p>
<p><button type="button" class="lx-btn ghost small">Open it anyway (recorded: practice)</button></p>
</div>
<div id="cka-solution-body" class="lx-xgrid lx-ck-gated cka-solution-body">
<!-- cka-solution:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The answer in one line</h3></header>
<p class="cka-big">Net present value to the school: <b>−$776,324</b> (2025 dollars, 25 years, 4% real). In present value the district pays $776,000 more than it saves.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">One-at-a-time swings put it between −$993,000 and −$560,000: no single swing changes its sign. Cumulative cash stays below zero in every year (lowest −$1,020,000), so there is no payback within 25 years.</p>
<p class="cka-dl"><a class="lx-btn small" href="../assets/learn/data/ck-a-worked.xlsx" download>Worked spreadsheet (.xlsx, live formulas)</a></p></div>
<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The numbers, step by step</h3></header><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts cka-sol">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Quantity</th><th scope="col">Worked value</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Energy charge (derived from EIA's average)</th><td class="n">$0.0637/kWh</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Solar output</th><td class="n">389,820 kWh a year (292,365 used, 97,455 sent out)</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Up-front cost</th><td class="n">$866,046 (2025 dollars; $792,500 in 2022 dollars × 1.0928)</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Bill saving, gross</th><td class="n">$31,965 a year = $18,624 energy + $2,924 exports + $10,800 demand − $382 losses</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Upkeep</th><td class="n">$14,972 a year ($4,645 solar, $10,327 battery)</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row"><span class="lx-term" data-term="annuity-factor">Annuity factor</span></th><td class="n">15.62 (25 years at 4%)</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Battery replacement, year 15</th><td class="n">$408,490; present value $226,820</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row"><span class="lx-term" data-term="residual-value">Residual value</span>, year 25</th><td class="n">$136,163 (5 of 15 years left, straight line); present value $51,077</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Net present value to the school</th><td class="n">−$776,324</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-hint">Check in the workbook: the year-by-year cash flow sums to the same −$776,324. The installed cost read as per kW-DC of solar is 7% below the two systems' separate costs, as the report says installing together saves.</p></div>
<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Who pays and who benefits</h3></header><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts cf-two cka-led">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Party</th><th scope="col">A year</th><th scope="col">Present value</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">The school district</th><td class="n" data-l="A year">$16,993</td><td class="n" data-l="Present value">−$776,324</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">The utility's other customers (at the next rate reset)</th><td class="n" data-l="A year">−$12,351</td><td class="n" data-l="Present value">−$192,941</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Federal taxpayers (no credit counted)</th><td class="n" data-l="A year">$0</td><td class="n" data-l="Present value">$0</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Resource view: all parties together</th><td class="n" data-l="A year">$4,642</td><td class="n" data-l="Present value">−$969,265</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<ul class="cka-list"><li><b>Gross against net:</b> of the school's $31,965 gross bill saving a year, $19,615 is a real cost the utility avoids; $12,351 is a <span class="lx-term" data-term="transfer">transfer</span> from its other customers.</li>
<li><b>Adds up:</b> school −$776,324 + other customers −$192,941 = resource view −$969,265.</li>
<li><b>Screening estimate:</b> the cost shift holds only under the brief's rate-reset assumption. It comes from the accounting of who pays, not from the model of the school's bill.</li>
<li><b>CO₂, not valued:</b> about 118 t a year at Kansas's 2024 average factor: an inventory number, not the change the project causes.</li>
<li><b>Resilience, not counted:</b> no <span class="lx-term" data-term="islanding">islanding</span> equipment is costed, so the battery gives no backup in an outage.</li>
<li><b>Jobs, not estimated:</b> installation is job-years of temporary work, not permanent jobs.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-xcard" id="cka-sens"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Sensitivity of the main result</h3></header><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts cf-two cka-sens">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Input</th><th scope="col">Low to high</th><th scope="col">NPV at low</th><th scope="col">NPV at high</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Up-front cost</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">$649,535 to $1,082,558</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$559,813</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$992,836</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Average electricity price</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">$0.0894 to $0.134 per kWh</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$876,265</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$676,384</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Battery's cut in the billed peak</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">30% to 90%</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$860,683</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$691,965</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Upkeep, solar and battery</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">$11,229 to $18,715 a year</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$717,850</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$834,798</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Demand charge (pre-project bill held)</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">$5 to $20 per kW-month</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$753,317</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$822,339</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Solar capacity factor</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">16.0% to 19.6%</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$809,986</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$742,663</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Share used at the school</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">60% to 90%</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$807,108</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$745,540</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Discount rate</th><td class="n" data-l="Low to high">2% to 7%</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at low">−$754,804</td><td class="n" data-l="NPV at high">−$790,985</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-hint">Sorted by swing. The demand-charge row varies the demand charge while holding the school's pre-project annual bill constant, so the energy charge falls as it rises.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Then the reduction in solar savings exceeds the increase in battery savings: the result falls.</p>

<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The points of the two written tasks</h3></header>
<p><b>Your boundary</b></p><ul class="cka-list"><li>Whose money: the school district's, from its electricity bill, the system's capital, upkeep and the battery's replacement.</li><li>Time and money: 25 years, real 2025 dollars, one real discount rate (4%), with costs from other dollar years converted.</li><li>Left out, and said so: tax credits, financing, resilience, CO2's value and solar wear (or a stated subset of these).</li><li>The other parties (the utility's other customers, federal taxpayers, the resource view) reported apart from the main result.</li></ul>
<p><b>Your log and your sensitivity</b></p><ul class="cka-list"><li>Every input has a value, a unit, a type (sourced, course data, illustrative, choice, derived) and a source or a reason.</li><li>Sourced values name the document, the table or page, and an as-of date.</li><li>Costs from different dollar years are converted to 2025 dollars with a stated index.</li><li>The main result is given as a range from the sensitivity, with the input that moves it most named.</li></ul>
</div>
```
